chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī, from some of his companions, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abū Khaythamah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, my father instructed me to wash him when he passed away, and he said to me: “Write, O my son.” Then he said: “They will command you to do contrary to what you are doing, so say to them: ‘This is the written instruction of my father, and I do not go beyond his statement.’” Then he said: “You begin by washing his hands, then perform wudu (ablution) for him as the wudu of salat (prayer), then you take lote leaves,” and he mentioned the hadith.

key_terms.أَغْسِلَهُ: to wash him ritually after death
key_terms.سِدْرًا: lote leaves used in washing the deceased
key_terms.كِتَابُ أَبِي: the written directive of my father
key_terms.وُضُوءَ الصَّلَاةِ: the manner of wudu used for salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does wudu (ablution) come before the ghusl of the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports instructions concerning the ghusl of the deceased, including washing the hands first and then performing wudu (ablution) as for salat (prayer). It also shows adherence to the explicit instruction of the Imam’s father in the face of opposing directions, highlighting the authority of transmitted guidance in funeral rites.
